Oe.bar_b_note: A naturalistic, well-furred hare with a moss cloak that clears the 1.80 m ruler would sit beside Palworld creatures, though the travel-role frame (a flat blue water slab on A, a floating hare carrying nothing on B) lets it down.

At.bar_b_note: A warm, appealing, earthy-palette elder with readable eyes and a clean silhouette matches the stylised finish, even if he is a little more cartoon than the naturalistic creatures.

Ll.bar_b_note: The mossy-shelled turtle has convincing plate and skin detail and is clearly larger than the trainer, but the travel frames (a turtle floating mid-air on A, a flat blue slab on B) look unfinished.

Ij.bar_b_note: Smeared, low-resolution ground and cliff textures, a uniform grass carpet and flat, shaft-less light sink it next to Palworld's dense fields, although B's aftermath staging (torn-down banners, an opened cage, smoke) carries each site better than A's.

Qv.bar_b_note: The storm wolf matches the owner's Tanglevolt bar in its standing frames, and B's glowing lightning veins hold through the faint, while on A the fur breaks into black-and-white blotches and the body floats in the faint frames.

Od.bar_b_note: A's braced timber frame, cap and stone footing read as a built wall, but the flat painted mountain backdrop, blurry low-poly rock and smeared path keep the scene below Palworld finish, and B's blown-out white panel looks like a placeholder.

Bw.bar_b_note: This is the same naturalistic moss-cloaked hare as Oe and reads well at small size, but the flat water slab on A and the floating carry on B undercut the travel role.

Wz.bar_b_note: This is the same strong mossy turtle as Ll, held back by the flat blue swim slab with its blown white edge on A and the mid-air carry pose with a detached shadow on B.

top_changes.change: Rebuild the Meadows world-frame materials and light: higher-resolution ground and cliff textures, grass grouped into groves and edges instead of a uniform carpet, warmer directional light with shafts and cool blue distance fog (Ij, Od).

Fix the travel-role presentation: a real water surface with a waterline on the creature instead of the flat blue slab with a blown white edge, and a grounded carrying pose with a visible load and an attached shadow instead of a creature floating mid-air (Oe, Bw, Ll, Wz).

Keep the creature material and ground contact through hurt and faint states (Qv A breaks into black-and-white blotches and floats), and on aftermath frames take down or wreck the enemy oxblood banners so each site reads as won (Ij A).
